stops.note: a funnel-shaped netted pond where tame ducks lured wild ones in, a device Dutch fowlers perfected
Dutch engineers draining the Fens brought the duck trap to England as a 'coy'; the Dutch article 'de' then fused on, and the word widened to any lure or trick
stops.meaning: a duck trap; later a lure

current_meaning: something used to lure a person or animal into a trap
